---
title: "Mirror the sbx \"balanced\" network policy as the msb default egress baseline"
status: accepted
date: 2026-08-07
decision_makers: ["Bret Mogilefsky"]
category: security
nist_controls: ["SC-7", "SC-8", "CM-2", "CM-6", "CM-7", "SA-8", "SA-15", "SI-10"]
impact_level: low
ato_relevance: yes-process
risk_treatment: mitigate
supersedes: []
---

> **Update (network tiers):** the `ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_EGRESS` toggle described
> below is now a **deprecated alias** for the neutral `ACQ_NETWORK_TIER`
> selector (`strict|balanced|open`, default `balanced`) defined by the
> agentic-coding-patterns network-tiers contract. `ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_EGRESS=1`
> maps to `balanced` (this baseline); `=0` now maps to `strict` — still
> deny-by-default with the kits' own hosts, NOT the former permissive
> no-deny-default behavior (an upgrade never silently loosens egress). See the
> `ACQ_NETWORK_TIER` section of [`docs/BACKEND_GUIDE.md`](../BACKEND_GUIDE.md).
> References to `ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_EGRESS=0` as "kit-only, no deny-default" below
> reflect the original toggle and are superseded by the `strict` tier mapping.
>
> **Update (ADR-0019):** the deny-default described below is scoped to **egress
> only** — the emitter uses `--net-default-egress deny`, not the symmetric
> `--net-default deny` this ADR originally specified. msb's `--net-default` sets
> **both** directions, which RST-rejected inbound traffic to create-time
> `-p HOST:GUEST` published ports. Ingress now keeps msb's baseline `allow`. See
> [ADR-0019](0019-msb-balanced-egress-is-egress-only.md). References to
> `--net-default deny` in the text below should be read as
> `--net-default-egress deny`.
>
> **Update (2026-08-17, msb 0.6.9):** acq now requires **msb >= 0.6.9**
> (`MIN_MSB_VERSION`). microsandbox 0.6.9 shipped the upstream release-build
> parser fix for the semantic `allow@dns` macro (the target-iterator advance was
> moved out of the `debug_assert` so it now runs on release binaries too). With
> the floor raised, the emitter no longer needs the expanded
> `allow@host:udp:53` + `allow@host:tcp:53` workaround: it emits the native
> **`allow@dns`** macro for the gateway-DNS grant in both the `balanced` and
> `strict` tiers. The "broken macro" / expanded-pair descriptions in the body
> below reflect the pre-0.6.9 workaround and are superseded by this note; the
> `docs/KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES.md` DNS failure mode is now resolved for supported
> versions.


## Decision

Give every msb sandbox the **same egress as the sbx `balanced` policy by
default**, composed on top of the kits' own `caps.network.allow`.

1. **Vendored host list.** Add `acq.backends/msb-balanced-hosts.txt` — a
   human-auditable, `#`-commentable file whose non-comment lines are a
   **verbatim mirror** of the `host:port` rows from `sbx policy inspect
   local-policy`. This file is the single source of truth an operator edits when
   sbx `balanced` changes. Keeping it a faithful mirror (no pre-translation)
   makes it trivially diffable against fresh `sbx policy inspect` output.

2. **Translation in one place.** The msb adapter
   (`_acq_msb_balanced_rules_into`, with helpers `_acq_msb_balanced_target` /
   `_acq_msb_balanced_port_ok`) translates each entry into an msb `--net-rule`
   per the msb grammar (`allow[:egress]@<target>[:<proto>[:<ports>]]`):
   - `**.host` (sbx multi-label glob) and `*.host` → msb domain-suffix `*.host`
     (msb suffixes match the apex and any subdomain at any depth, so collapsing
     `**.` → `*.` loses no coverage).
   - `:PORT` → `:tcp:<port>` (sbx `balanced` is TCP; a host listed on both `:80`
     and `:443` yields **two** rules, preserved per-port).
   - `crl*.digicert.com` (an intra-label glob msb **cannot** express) → broadened
     to the parent suffix `*.digicert.com`, with a one-time warning recording the
     widening. This preserves CRL / certificate-revocation reachability on `:80`,
     a real TLS-path dependency, at the cost of a slightly wider match than sbx.
   - A leading gateway-DNS grant is emitted so the guest can resolve the
     allowed hosts — under `--net-default deny` the high-level DNS auto-grant
     does not apply, so DNS must be granted explicitly. This pairs with the
     existing `--dns-nameserver`. The emitter uses msb's semantic **`allow@dns`**
     macro (the gateway `host` group on UDP/TCP port 53). This macro was broken
     on released msb builds up to and including 0.6.8 — its parser advanced past
     the `dns` target only inside a `debug_assert_eq!`, which is compiled out of
     a release binary, so the `dns` token was re-read as the protocol slot and
     `msb create` failed with `the dns target supports tcp, udp, or any, not
     dns`. microsandbox 0.6.9 fixed this (the release-build parser fix moves the
     iterator advance out of the assert), and acq requires msb >= 0.6.9
     (`MIN_MSB_VERSION`), so the macro is safe to emit directly. (Before the
     floor was raised, the emitter used the expanded
     `allow@host:udp:53` + `allow@host:tcp:53` pair as a workaround; see the
     0.6.9 update note above.)

3. **Restrict, don't merely widen.** At create, when the baseline is enabled the
   adapter emits `--net-default deny` **plus** the generated `allow@…` rules, so
   egress is *restricted to* the balanced set (deny-by-default + allowlist) —
   genuine parity with sbx `balanced`, not "allow-all with extras". The kit, npm,
   and secret-binding rules are all `allow@…` and compose correctly under the
   deny default.

4. **Toggle, on by default.** `ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_EGRESS` (default on) enables the
   baseline; `0`/`false`/`no`/`off`/empty (case-insensitive) disables it and
   falls back to kit-only egress (no `--net-default deny` is emitted in that
   mode). `ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_HOSTS_FILE` overrides the list path for a
   site-specific set.
normalized_decision: Make msb's default neutral network tier balanced, mirroring the curated sbx balanced egress set through a vendored auditable host list plus backend translation; enforce egress deny-by-default with allowlisted balanced, kit, npm, secret, and native allow@dns rules; require msb >=0.6.9 for the repaired DNS macro; keep ingress default-allow per ADR-0019; treat ACQ_MSB_BALANCED_EGRESS as a deprecated alias mapping 1 to balanced and 0 to strict rather than to a permissive no-deny mode.
candidate_rule: Supported msb balanced mode emits an egress deny default plus the translated allowlist and native DNS grant; network-tier aliases cannot silently loosen egress.
human_notes: Draft human reference. Current-state normalization follows the source's three top-of-record update notes (network tiers, ADR-0019 egress-only refinement, and msb >=0.6.9 native allow@dns). ONTOLOGY_GAP: those notes replace individual clauses without superseding the active ADR as a whole.
